statement: For every integer r>=2 and all positive integers a,c,b, define [a]_q=sum_{i=0}^{a-1}q^i and [b]_(q^r)=sum_{j=0}^{b-1}q^(rj). The full integer-indexed coefficient sequence of [a]_q[c]_q[b]_(q^r), including zero coefficients, is weakly unimodal if and only if r divides a, or r divides c, or b<=1+floor(a/r)+floor(c/r). The disjunction is inclusive and factor-1 cases are included. This is exactly the k=2 restriction of the original Conjecture 5.4; no assertion resolving its other parameter ranges is submitted.
contribution: A self-contained proposed proof of the exact two-factor criterion at arbitrary stretch, extending Connelly-Ito-Martinez-Shevchenko-Yang Proposition 4.5 from r=2 to every r>=2. The new sufficient step closes the clipped-interval inequality by floor subadditivity and a midpoint/residue estimate; an explicit negative-difference witness proves necessity. Divisibility and k=1 boundary cases are known and are not claimed as new. The complete original conjunction remains unresolved. The bounded current primary-source comparison found no equivalent extension in the inspected evidence, without a priority guarantee; fresh mathematical and contribution review is requested.
